newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn backs attack on Iraq, demands Baghdad pullout.
newsitem.headline: Bonn backs attack on Iraq, demands Baghdad pullout.

text.p: Germany backed U.S. cruise missile attacks against targets in Iraq on Tuesday, and said it expected Baghdad to pull its troops out of the north of the country at once and stop attacks on Kurdish civilians.
"The Iraqi side violated the (Kurdish) safety zone in northern Iraq and caused a great amount of bloodshed," Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel told reporters.
"In the view of the German government, the U.S. response was appropriate and justified."

Early on Tuesday, the U.S. Navy and air force B-52 bombers launched cruise missile strikes against air defence and communications targets in southern Iraq in response to Iraq's military attacks against Kurds in the north of the country.
Iraq said five people were killed and 19 wounded in the attacks.

German government spokesman Peter Hausmann, visiting Kiev with Chancellor Helmut Kohl, said Germany had from the outset condemned Iraq's incursion into the United Nations-implemented no-fly zone in northern Iraq.
"The federal government expects that everything will be done in the current situation to avoid an escalation," he added.
"In particular, it expects Iraq to withdraw its troops immediately and completely and cease all use of violence against the Kurdish civilian population."
Kinkel told reporters he would discuss the matter at length with U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher, who visits Germany on Friday.
